profile.name: Anna Williams
profile.overview: An extremely aggressive, high-risk high-reward character built around dangerous 50/50s and mix-ups. In Tekken 8 she carries a bazooka-mace ("Lovely Tom"): weapon attacks deal chip damage and can inflict the Fragile debuff, which makes the opponent take chip damage from any attack. Her Hammer Chance (HAM) and Pleasure Time (TOM) stances lead into weapon attacks with better range and tracking, and Chaos Judgement (CJM) parries lows and throws.
profile.playstyle: Rushdown with stance mix-ups and plus frames. When opponents read her, she gets punished hard, so the game plan is to stay unpredictable, use plus-frame moves to keep the turn, and be disciplined about her many unsafe options.
strengths: Mix-ups: an unseeable 50/50 from crouch plus many stance and string options
Strong lows with good damage and frames on hit, several leading to follow-ups
Many plus-frame tools that keep her in the opponent's face
High chip damage from weapon attacks and the Fragile debuff
Big reads: CJM stance and her reversal stop opponents in their tracks
weaknesses: Subpar punishment: no i11 or i12 standing punisher; i10 options are weak or short-ranged
Gambler's tools: an unconfirmable i11 CH launch string that is launch punishable on block; stance mix-ups that can be interrupted
Her crouch mix-ups can be sidewalked to the left and many key pokes are linear

stances.name: Hammer Chance
stances.note: Several moves (e.g. 2,2, uf+2/u+2, db+4, b+4) transition to HAM automatically on hit.

stances.name: Chaos Judgement
stances.note: Per Wavu, CJM auto-launches low attacks and reverses throws, but you cannot block while in it. TOM.3 also enters it.

stances.name: Pleasure Time
stances.note: db+2 and HAM.2,2 transition to TOM automatically on hit.

heat: Gains extra hits on 1,2,1,2, f,f,F+3,2 and CJM.3,2
Gains uf+3 and FC.df+2 follow-up extensions (H. moves in the move list)

keyMoves.summary: Jab: her fastest standing attack.
keyMoves.purpose: Interrupt the opponent, check them up close, and start i10 punishes.
keyMoves.use: When you are slightly minus or neutral at close range, or when you need the fastest possible response.
keyMoves.avoid: At mid range (short reach) or against crouching opponents: it is a high and gets ducked.
keyMoves.counterplay: Opponents crouch (duck) under it and punish with a while-standing launcher if they read it.
keyMoves.afterBlock: You keep a small advantage: continue pressure or go into a string.
keyMoves.afterHit: You are plus and can keep attacking.
keyMoves.afterEvade: If ducked, you are at risk of a ws punish; be careful about repeating it.
keyMoves.gamePlan: The universal reset button. Use it to stop opponents mashing after their minus moves.

keyMoves.summary: Her listed i10 standing punisher (Wavu punisher table).
keyMoves.purpose: Guaranteed damage after blocking -10 moves.
keyMoves.use: Whenever you block a move that is -10 to -12 and you have nothing faster that fits.
keyMoves.avoid: Against ducking opponents at neutral: both hits are high.
keyMoves.counterplay: Crouching under it. Range is short, so long-range -10 moves can push you out of reach.
keyMoves.afterBlock: Slightly minus; don't keep pressing buttons carelessly.
keyMoves.afterEvade: Ducked highs give the opponent a free ws punish.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Your bread-and-butter small punish. Anna lacks i11/i12 punishers, so learn when to use this versus df+1 or f+2,3.

keyMoves.summary: Fast mid check (Wavu lists it as her standing mid check).
keyMoves.purpose: Hit opponents who crouch or press buttons, safely.
keyMoves.use: When the opponent likes to duck your highs or crouch-jab after your moves.
keyMoves.avoid: When you need big damage; it is a check, not a combo starter.
keyMoves.counterplay: Blocking it and sidestepping its follow-ups.
keyMoves.afterBlock: Nearly even: you can continue or reset.
keyMoves.afterHit: Plus on hit; keep your turn.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Use it to make your highs and lows threatening: opponents who duck everything get hit by this.

keyMoves.summary: Step-in uppercut launcher.
keyMoves.purpose: Her standard i15 launch punisher and the starter of her main combo.
keyMoves.use: Punish moves that are -15 or worse on block (Wavu punisher table), and as a whiff punisher at close range.
keyMoves.avoid: Throwing it out raw in neutral: it is punishable on block.
keyMoves.counterplay: Blocking it and punishing with a -12 punisher; sidestepping.
keyMoves.afterBlock: You are punishable: expect to take a hit.
keyMoves.afterHit: Launch! Go into the regular launch combo.
keyMoves.afterEvade: Big recovery if it whiffs; you can be launched.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Your reward for blocking launch-punishable moves. Practise the BnB from this starter first.

keyMoves.summary: Standing i14 punisher that wall splats (Wavu splat list).
keyMoves.purpose: Punish -14 moves for more damage than 1,2 and carry/splat near the wall.
keyMoves.use: Against -14 moves (Wavu punisher table), especially when the opponent's back is near a wall.
keyMoves.avoid: As a random poke at range: the second hit is a high.
keyMoves.counterplay: Ducking the high second hit after blocking the first.
keyMoves.afterBlock: Minus but generally safe; reset to defence.
keyMoves.afterHit: Near the wall it splats: follow up with a wall combo.
keyMoves.afterEvade: Ducked second hit leaves you open.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Your best mid-size punish near walls.

keyMoves.summary: i14 Heat Engager, usable as a standing or crouching -14 punisher.
keyMoves.purpose: Punish -14 moves and enter Heat at the same time.
keyMoves.use: Punishing -14 moves when you want to start Heat, standing or after blocking a low (Wavu: can be done from ws).
keyMoves.avoid: In neutral: it is launch punishable on block per the frame data.
keyMoves.counterplay: Block it and launch.
keyMoves.afterBlock: Severely minus: you will likely be launched.
keyMoves.afterHit: Heat engaged; the Heat Dash follow-up keeps pressure.
keyMoves.gamePlan: A punish that also turns on your Heat resources.

keyMoves.summary: Assassin's Dagger ("Blue Spark" on Wavu): i13 high that launches on counter hit.
keyMoves.purpose: Interrupt opponents who press buttons; plus on block per the frame data.
keyMoves.use: When you expect the opponent to attack: a counter hit launches.
keyMoves.avoid: Against ducking opponents: it is a high.
keyMoves.counterplay: Duck it and punish, or don't press buttons into it.
keyMoves.afterHit: Plus on normal hit; on counter hit, combo.
keyMoves.gamePlan: One of her best key techs (Wavu lists it). Learn the input until it is automatic.

keyMoves.summary: Crouch jab: her listed -10 crouching punisher.
keyMoves.purpose: Fast check while crouching; ducks highs.
keyMoves.use: After blocking a low that is -10, or to stop opponents who are plus but slow.
keyMoves.avoid: Expecting damage: it is a small hit.
keyMoves.counterplay: Mids beat crouching.
keyMoves.afterHit: Plus on hit; you are still crouching (consider ws moves next).
keyMoves.gamePlan: Minimum punish from crouch when nothing better fits.

keyMoves.summary: Fast while-standing mid; her -11 crouching punisher (Wavu).
keyMoves.purpose: Punish lows and stop crouching pressure.
keyMoves.use: After blocking -11 lows, or rising from crouch against opponents who press.
keyMoves.avoid: When you need launch damage.
keyMoves.counterplay: Blocking it; it is safe for Anna.
keyMoves.afterHit: Plus on hit; Wavu notes a CH launch with Heat Dash.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Your reliable mid-size crouching punish.

keyMoves.summary: While-standing launcher.
keyMoves.purpose: Launch after blocking lows that are -16 or worse (Wavu punisher table).
keyMoves.use: After crouch-blocking very unsafe lows, then go into the BnB.
keyMoves.avoid: Using it raw in neutral: it is punishable on block.
keyMoves.counterplay: Blocking it.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Turn blocked lows into full combos. Requires a clean crouch → release → press input.

keyMoves.summary: Hopkick: jumping mid launcher.
keyMoves.purpose: Launch from crouch punishes (-18 per Wavu) and jump over lows.
keyMoves.use: Crouching punish for very unsafe lows; anti-low read.
keyMoves.avoid: Neutral spam: it is launch punishable on block.
keyMoves.counterplay: Block and launch.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Highest-damage crouching punish.

keyMoves.summary: Stature kick: low that transitions to HAM on hit.
keyMoves.purpose: Low damage and stance pressure.
keyMoves.use: Against opponents who stand and block patiently.
keyMoves.avoid: When they are ready to block low: it is punishable.
keyMoves.counterplay: Crouch-block and punish with a ws move.
keyMoves.afterHit: Plus; HAM transition (cancel with B per Wavu) lets you continue.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Low half of her mix-ups at mid range.

keyMoves.summary: Slow low sweep that launches on hit (snake edge type).
keyMoves.purpose: Big low reward against opponents who only stand.
keyMoves.use: Sparingly, as a read on a patient blocker.
keyMoves.avoid: Against players who react: it is slow and launch punishable on block.
keyMoves.counterplay: Block low and launch.
keyMoves.gamePlan: High-risk tool: once they respect it, your mids work better.

keyMoves.summary: i11 counter-hit launch string (all highs per Wavu).
keyMoves.purpose: Interrupt with a fast CH launcher.
keyMoves.use: When the opponent tends to press buttons after being slightly minus.
keyMoves.avoid: As a habit: Wavu notes it cannot be confirmed and is launch punishable on block.
keyMoves.counterplay: Block it and launch, or duck the highs.
keyMoves.gamePlan: A gamble tool. Use it when you have conditioned the opponent to press.

keyMoves.summary: Hammer Chance (HAM) stance entry.
keyMoves.purpose: Enter HAM for weapon attacks with better range and tracking.
keyMoves.use: To start stance mix-ups and to cancel into other stances (HAM cancel is a Wavu key tech).
keyMoves.avoid: When the opponent is ready to interrupt the stance.
keyMoves.counterplay: Interrupting the stance with fast moves.
keyMoves.gamePlan: The gateway to HAM.1/HAM.2 options and stance cancels.

keyMoves.summary: Chaos Judgement (CJM) stance entry: parries lows and throws.
keyMoves.purpose: Read lows and throws; auto-launch lows per Wavu.
keyMoves.use: When you expect a low or a throw.
keyMoves.avoid: Against mids: you cannot block in CJM.
keyMoves.counterplay: Hit it with a mid.
keyMoves.afterHit: On a parried low, Anna launches automatically (Wavu).
keyMoves.afterEvade: If they don't attack, you have CJM options.
keyMoves.gamePlan: A read tool, not a defensive habit.

keyMoves.summary: Ocelot Claw: mid that transitions to TOM on hit.
keyMoves.purpose: Mid that leads to TOM; launches on counter hit.
keyMoves.use: Mid-range pressure; CH db+2 → TOM.2 is a documented mini-combo.
keyMoves.avoid: When the opponent is ready to punish: it is minus on block.
keyMoves.counterplay: Block and punish if fast enough.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Entry point to Pleasure Time pressure.

keyMoves.summary: Attack Reversal: parries high or mid punches and kicks (Wavu).
keyMoves.purpose: Defensive read against expected highs/mids.
keyMoves.use: When the opponent repeats a predictable punch or kick.
keyMoves.avoid: Against lows, throws and moves that can't be reversed.
keyMoves.counterplay: Throws, lows, or simply not attacking.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Situational read; don't rely on it.

keyMoves.summary: Heat Smash.
keyMoves.purpose: Big mid during Heat; transitions to an attack throw on hit.
keyMoves.use: During Heat to end a round or force a big guess.
keyMoves.avoid: Using it carelessly; check its block frames.
keyMoves.counterplay: Blocking it.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Heat resource spender.

keyMoves.summary: Rage Art.
keyMoves.purpose: Armoured comeback move when in Rage.
keyMoves.use: As a read when the opponent is about to attack and you are in Rage.
keyMoves.avoid: Against a blocking opponent: very unsafe on block.
keyMoves.counterplay: Block it and launch.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Last resort; save it for clear reads.

keyMoves.summary: Generic throw (broken with 1).
keyMoves.purpose: Beat opponents who block a lot.
keyMoves.use: When they are blocking your pressure up close.
keyMoves.avoid: Against crouching opponents: standing throws whiff.
keyMoves.counterplay: Break with 1, or crouch.
keyMoves.gamePlan: Forces opponents to stop just blocking.

combos.name: CH Ocelot Claw → TOM.2
combos.situation: Your db+2 lands as a counter hit (it launches on CH per the frame data). db+2 transitions to TOM automatically on hit.
mistakes: Pressing 2 before the counter hit actually lands: only follow up when you see the CH.
Holding a direction when pressing TOM.2: just press 2.

combos.name: Sudden Storm follow-up
combos.situation: uf+3 hits (knockdown on hit per the frame data). Follow with u+2 (an alternate input of uf+2, Bane Stinger).
mistakes: Pressing uf+2 instead: the source lists u+2.
Waiting too long after uf+3 lands.

combos.name: CH low kick > back spin chop → 1,2,1
combos.situation: The second hit of d+4,1 counter hits. Wavu lists 1,2,1 or 2,3 as follow-ups.
mistakes: Starting the follow-up before the CH lands.

combos.name: CH low kick > back spin chop → 2,3
combos.situation: Same starter as above with the shorter 2,3 follow-up.

combos.name: CH Open Sesame → f+2,3
combos.situation: 1+2 or CJM.1 lands as a counter hit. (Wavu also lists CH d+3,2 near the wall as a starter.)
mistakes: Pressing 2 without holding forward (gives a different move).

combos.name: Headless Horseman → u+2
combos.situation: f,F+2 hits (or one of the listed counter-hit starters). Follow with u+2.
mistakes: Missing the f,F motion: tap forward, then forward again and hold while pressing 2.

combos.name: Regular launch BnB
combos.situation: Any regular launch (df+2 punish, uf+4/ws2 crouching punish). Wavu's Bread n' Butter for Anna.
combos.route: 2,2 HAM.2,1 u+2 HAM.2,2T! (TOM.3) CJM u/f+3 d/b+2 TOM.2
mistakes: Pressing HAM.2 too early: 2,2 must hit so Anna transitions to HAM automatically.
Forgetting that u+2 also transitions to HAM on hit: the next 2 is HAM.2.
After HAM.2,2 (tornado) Anna is in TOM: TOM.3 enters CJM, then uf+3 from CJM.
Rushing d/b+2 → TOM.2: db+2 must hit before you press 2.

stepTips.TOM.3: TOM.3 is Chaos Judgement from Pleasure Time: it puts Anna into CJM for the next step.

source.name: Wavu Wiki: Anna combos (Bread n' butter)

combos.name: CH Blue Spark (qcf+1) staple
combos.situation: qcf+1 lands as a counter hit (launches on CH).
combos.route: u/f+3 u+2 HAM.2,1 b+4 HAM.2,2T! (TOM.3) CJM.u/f+3 d/b+2 TOM.2
mistakes: Not confirming the counter hit before continuing.
b+4 transitions to HAM automatically on hit: the following 2,2 is HAM.2,2.

lessons.title: Who is Anna?
objectives: Understand Anna's high-risk, high-reward game plan
Recognise her key moves and their hit levels
lessons.explanation:
Anna wins by **staying on top of the opponent**: plus-frame moves, stance transitions (HAM, TOM, CJM) and dangerous 50/50s. Her weakness is defence: **no i11/i12 standing punisher** and many moves that are punishable if read.

As a beginner, focus on three things: block well, punish what you can with 1,2 / f+2,3 / df+2, and learn one reliable combo. Stance mix-ups come later, once you can execute them under pressure.
lessons.success: Mastery threshold on both quizzes.
review: Highs can be ducked; mids can't. Know which of her pokes are highs.

lessons.title: Essential pokes
objectives: Execute 1, 1,2, df+1, d+1, f+2,3 and db+4 cleanly
Know which are safe
lessons.explanation:
Pokes are fast, low-commitment attacks that win small exchanges.

- **1 / 1,2**: fastest, highs
- **df+1**: mid check, beats ducking
- **d+1**: crouch jab, ducks highs
- **f+2,3**: strong punish and wall splat
- **db+4**: low that transitions to HAM on hit

Open each move in the Move Library to see verified frame data and coach notes.

challenge.note: Clean diagonal inputs: df and db, not d.

lessons.success: Inputs at the mastery threshold.
review: Most failures here are diagonals: check the input log for d instead of df.

lessons.title: Anna's throws
objectives: Perform 1+3, 2+4 and db+1+2 (Queen's Reward)
Break throws in the simulation
lessons.explanation:
Throws beat players who just block. Anna has the generic **1+3** and **2+4** throws plus command throws such as **db+1+2** (Queen's Reward). Check the Move Library for damage and break information.

On defence, break 1+3 with 1 and 2+4 with 2.
lessons.success: Throw inputs and breaks at the required rates.
review: Throws must be pressed together within a couple of frames.

lessons.title: Stage 1 test: foundations
objectives: Prove you can read notation and execute Anna's basic inputs
lessons.explanation: Mixed inputs and a frame-data quiz. Pass to unlock Stage 2.
lessons.success: Mastery threshold on both parts.
review: Retry the lesson whose inputs you missed.

lessons.title: Launchers: df+2, ws2, uf+4
objectives: Execute each launcher cleanly
Know which launcher to use standing versus crouching
lessons.explanation:
A launcher pops the opponent into the air for a combo.

- **df+2**: standing launch punisher (-15)
- **ws2**: while standing after blocking a low (-16)
- **uf+4**: hopkick, crouching punish (-18)

All three are punishable on block, so use them as **punishers**, not pokes.

The ws2 input: hold down (block low), release, and press 2 as you rise.
lessons.success: Inputs and quiz at the mastery threshold.
review: ws2 fails if you are still holding down when you press.

lessons.title: First combos: short and reliable
objectives: Land two- and three-input mini-combos consistently
lessons.explanation:
Start with Wavu's mini-combos: short follow-ups that are easy to land.

- **CH db+2 → TOM.2**
- **uf+3 → u+2**
- **CH (d+4),1 → 2,3**

The Combo Lab shows every step with controller icons. Use **Slow** mode first, then **Consistency** mode.
lessons.success: Required consecutive clean executions.
review: Most early failures are pressing the follow-up before the starter finishes. Watch the step timeline.

lessons.title: Standing punishment
objectives: Pick the right punisher for -10, -13, -14 and -15
Punish in the simulation on time
lessons.explanation:
Anna's standing punishers (Wavu punisher table):

- **-10**: 1,2 or 2,3
- **-13**: b+2,2
- **-14**: f+2,3 / 3+4 / 3,2
- **-15**: df+2 (launch)

She has **nothing faster than i13 that does more than 1,2**, so recognising -14/-15 moves matters a lot for her damage.
lessons.success: Quiz at the mastery threshold, punish rate at the drill pass rate.
review: 'Too slow' means you pressed after the window: buffer during blockstun.
'Not guaranteed' means your move is slower than the window.

lessons.title: Crouching punishment
objectives: Punish blocked lows with d+1, ws3, ws1,2, ws2 and uf+4
lessons.explanation:
After you crouch-block a low you can't use standing moves immediately. Anna's crouching punishers (Wavu):

- **-10**: d+1
- **-11**: ws3
- **-13**: ws1,2
- **-14**: 3+4 (from ws)
- **-16**: ws2 (launch)
- **-18**: uf+4 (launch)
lessons.success: Inputs at threshold and drill pass rate.
review: The ws timing: release down and press almost together.

lessons.title: Basic neutral: spacing and checks
objectives: Understand close, mid and long range for Anna
Practise basic neutral habits in Tekken 8
lessons.explanation:
Neutral is the moment when neither player has advantage. Coach advice for beginners:

- **Close range**: jab and df+1 checks, throws, short strings.
- **Mid range**: low pokes like db+4, f,F+2 to close in, qcf+1 to catch buttons.
- **Long range**: move (backdash, sidestep) and wait for whiffs to punish.

Because many of Anna's options are linear, the opponent's sidestep left is a real threat: mix in moves that track (check the tracking column on the source).

This lesson's challenge happens in Tekken 8: the app cannot see the game, so you confirm the checklist yourself.

items: Play 3 matches (ranked, player match or CPU) focusing only on blocking and punishing
Watch one replay and note one move you could have punished
In Practice mode, set the dummy to sidestep after a jab and find which of your moves still hit

lessons.success: Quiz at threshold and the in-game checklist confirmed.
review: If you lose neutral constantly, slow down: block more, attack less.

lessons.title: Stage 2 test: core combat
objectives: Punish and combo under test conditions
lessons.explanation: A punishment drill plus a mini-combo consistency check. Pass to unlock Stage 3.
lessons.success: Combo consistency and drill pass rate.
review: Check the Progress page for your most common error.

lessons.title: Bread-and-butter combo
objectives: Land Anna's regular launch BnB in the Combo Lab
lessons.explanation:
Anna's BnB from Wavu: **2,2 HAM.2,1 u+2 HAM.2,2T! (TOM.3) CJM u/f+3 d/b+2 TOM.2** after df+2, uf+4, ws2 or CJM.uf+4.

The stance flow is the key: 2,2 → HAM automatically; u+2 → HAM again; HAM.2,2 → tornado and TOM; TOM.3 → CJM; db+2 → TOM.

Learn it in pieces with **Step-by-step** and **Slow** modes. Only the input order and timing can be checked here; whether every hit connects must be confirmed in Tekken 8 Practice mode.
lessons.success: Required consecutive clean executions.
review: Use the Progress page's 'weakest transition' to drill the exact step you drop.

lessons.title: Counter-hit tools
objectives: Execute qcf+1, 4,2,1+2 and db+2
Know when each is worth the risk
lessons.explanation:
Counter hit = hitting the opponent while they are starting an attack. Anna has strong CH launchers:

- **qcf+1** (Blue Spark): i13 high, plus on block, launches on CH
- **4,2,1+2**: i11, launches on CH but launch punishable on block and not confirmable (Wavu)
- **db+2**: mid, launches on CH, leads to TOM

Use them when the opponent **likes to press buttons** after being minus. Against patient blockers, they are risk without reward.
lessons.success: Inputs at threshold and consistent CH follow-up.
review: qcf+1 needs d, df, f in order: check the input log.

lessons.title: Lows and pressure
objectives: Know which lows are safe and which are launch punishable
Execute db+4, d+4,1 and db+3
lessons.explanation:
Lows force the opponent to guess. The frame data tells you how much each low risks:

- **db+4**: stature kick, punishable but plus on hit with HAM transition
- **d+4,1**: low into high follow-up
- **db+3**: slow sweep that launches on hit but is launch punishable on block

Pressure means making the opponent guess while keeping your risk acceptable.
lessons.success: Quiz and inputs at threshold.
review: Don't throw the same low repeatedly: opponents will start blocking it.

lessons.title: Whiff punishment
objectives: Punish whiffed moves within their recovery
lessons.explanation:
When an opponent's attack **misses** (whiffs), they are stuck in recovery. Hitting them then is a whiff punish.

For Anna, df+2 (launch) and f+2,3 are strong whiff punishers at close range; qcf+1 reaches further. Backdash to make moves whiff, then punish.

The simulation measures timing only. Real whiff punishment also depends on range and the opponent's recovery animation, so practise it in Tekken 8 too.
lessons.success: Drill pass rate.
review: Pressing during the whiff's active frames gets you counter-hit; wait for the recovery.

lessons.title: Stage 3 test: reliable execution
objectives: BnB consistency and crouching punishment
lessons.explanation: Land the BnB repeatedly and punish lows. Pass to unlock Stage 4.
lessons.success: Consistency and drill pass rate.
review: Drill the specific BnB transition you fail most (see Progress).

lessons.title: Stances: HAM, TOM and CJM
objectives: Enter each stance and use its main options
Understand which moves transition automatically
lessons.explanation:
- **HAM (Hammer Chance)**: f+3, or automatically after moves like 2,2, uf+2/u+2, db+4 (on hit) and b+4. HAM.1 is a Heat Engager; HAM.2,2 tornados in combos.
- **TOM (Pleasure Time)**: after db+2, ws1,2 and HAM.2,2 on hit.
- **CJM (Chaos Judgement)**: b+3 or TOM.3. Parries lows and throws, but **cannot block** (Wavu).

These transitions come from Wavu's move notes; open any move in the Move Library to see them.
lessons.success: Inputs and quiz at threshold.
review: In CJM you cannot block: never sit in it against a mid.

lessons.title: Counter-hit qcf+1 staple
objectives: Land the CH qcf+1 staple route
lessons.explanation:
Wavu's staple after **CH qcf+1**: u/f+3 u+2 HAM.2,1 b+4 HAM.2,2T! (TOM.3) CJM.u/f+3 d/b+2 TOM.2.

It adds b+4 (which transitions to HAM on hit) before the tornado. If it is too hard, fall back to the BnB.
lessons.success: Required consecutive clean executions.
review: Confirm in Tekken 8 Practice (dummy: counter hit on) that each hit connects.

lessons.title: Wall carry and wall splats
objectives: Know Anna's wall-splat moves
Find and save a wall combo in Tekken 8
lessons.explanation:
Wall splats keep the opponent stuck on the wall for an extra combo. Anna's splat tools per Wavu: **f+2,3** (standing, i14) and **qcf+2,1** (standing or crouching, i16).

Wavu's Anna wall-combo section is **currently empty**, so this app does not invent one. Use the checklist to find a route in Practice mode and add it to your notes.

items: In Tekken 8 Practice, wall splat the dummy with f+2,3
Find a short follow-up that connects after the splat and note its damage
Repeat it 5 times in a row in Practice

lessons.success: Inputs at threshold and checklist confirmed.
review: Wall combos scale damage heavily: short, reliable routes are fine.

lessons.title: Defence under pressure
objectives: Block mix-ups, break throws and punish in a mixed scenario
lessons.explanation:
The mixed-pressure bot chooses between unsafe attacks (punish them), safe attacks (block and don't press), lows and throws. It **adapts**: it uses more of what you fail.

This is a timing and decision simulation, not Tekken 8's engine.
lessons.success: Drill pass rate.
review: If 'pressed into safe move' is your top error, practise blocking twice before acting.

lessons.title: Using Heat
objectives: Know Anna's Heat Engagers and Heat-only extensions
lessons.explanation:
Anna's Heat Engagers (Wavu): **HAM.1, 3+4, FC.df+1, CJM.2,1, f,F+3,2**. In Heat she gains extra hits on 1,2,1,2, f,f,F+3,2 and CJM.3,2, and the uf+3 / FC.df+2 extensions (shown as `H.` moves).

Heat moves consume Heat time per the move notes; check the Move Library before relying on them.

items: In Tekken 8 Practice, activate Heat with 3+4 and land H.2+3
Note how much Heat time each Heat move consumes

lessons.success: Inputs at threshold and checklist confirmed.
review: Heat is once per round; spend it where it converts to damage or a round win.

lessons.title: Stage 4 test: advanced play
objectives: Stance inputs, advanced route and defence
lessons.explanation: Pass to unlock Stage 5.
lessons.success: Consistency and drill pass rate.
review: Use Review sessions on the dashboard for decayed skills.

lessons.title: Scenario challenges
objectives: Make correct decisions under a high-pressure adaptive bot
lessons.explanation: Tournament play is about decisions under stress. Set the drill difficulty to **Hard** (shorter reaction windows) and pass the mixed scenario.
lessons.success: Drill pass rate on any difficulty; Hard is recommended.
review: Look at your error breakdown: fix the single biggest category first.

lessons.title: Matchup preparation
objectives: Build a punishment sheet for your most common opponents
lessons.explanation:
Competitive preparation means knowing **what to punish and with what** for the characters you meet most. Use the Punishment Trainer with the opponent filter, and the in-game checklist below.

The app currently includes frame data for Anna and Armor King only; more characters can be imported from Wavu Wiki (see Settings → Data).

items: List the 3 characters you lose to most
For each, record 2 unsafe moves in Practice and find your best punish
Practise those punishes with the dummy's recording playback

lessons.success: Quiz at threshold and checklist confirmed.
review: Revisit this lesson each patch: frame data changes.

lessons.title: Final test: competitive readiness
objectives: Execution, punishment and decision-making together
lessons.explanation: The full exam: BnB consistency and the adaptive mixed scenario.
lessons.success: Both parts at the required level.
review: Keep using daily review sessions: skills decay without practice.
